newsitem.title: USA: Scotts Co to take $17.6 mln FY96 charge.
newsitem.headline: Scotts Co to take $17.6 mln FY96 charge.

text.p: Scotts Co said on Thursday that it expected fiscal 1996 earnings to breakeven, before $17.6 million in non-recurring charges.

The company said in a statement that a previously announced $8.6 million charge and a $9 million charge to be taken in the fourth quarter, would result in a net loss of between $0.70 and $0.75 per share.
Scott also said it received a temporary waiver of a debt covenant on interest coverage from its lenders.
The First Call mean estimate for the fourth quarter was loss of $0.21 per share and for the full year was a profit of $0.32 per share.
The estimated loss would be after payment of a preferred stock dividend, Scotts said, adding it would take the $9 million charge for restructuring and severance plant closings and asset write-downs.

Charges reflected a series of restructuring efforts introduced in 1996, including the redesign of trade programs, the reduction of inventory and receivables, and a reduction in capital expenditure, it said.
Scotts also said it was confident it would again comply with the covenant by the end of the 1997 second quarter, when the spring selling season began.

"While these actions have short-term negative impact for 1996, they are part of a firm foundation for long-term profitable growth in 1997 and beyond," Scotts Chairman, President and Chief Executive Charles Berger said in a statement.
The company said it had new marketing programs in place for 1997 and it expected trade inventories to be substantially reduced from prior year levels as a result.

It said restructuring initiatives in 1996 should result in annualized savings in excess of $13 million and fiscal 1996 expenditures were reduced to about $19 million from original plans of $28 million.
Substantial progress had also been been made in reducing receivable by about $60 million, compared with September 30, 1995, Scotts said.
Berger also said the company expected to generate about $45 million in free cash flow for the year.

He said, relative to the positive cash flow, the board of directors has approved negotiations on the purchase of of the remaining interest in UK-based Miracle Garden Care Ltd. Scotts owns one-third of Miracle Garden.
